card.title: We Keep Switching Places
card.instruction: Return to a familiar relationship pattern, then reverse who performs each role whenever the scene reaches similar pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tap's leaking again. Give me the spanner before you start pricing lifeboats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've found the valve. You look terrified.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you fix it. I'll keep the towels ready for when the kitchen goes under.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The valve's stuck. What if I snap it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the spanner. You take the towels; you've reached the sinking-kitchen stage.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 fixer mocks B's panic, A3 becomes the catastrophizer when B finds control and A5 resumes fixing when B panics.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 competence and fear observation cause A3 handover; B4 stuck valve causes A5 reverse handover.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a repair route and B4 has a specific reason to fear breakage.

heightening.evidence: B4 shared pressure transfers panic back to B, so A5 takes the spanner and assigns the towels.

specificity.evidence: A1 recurring tap leak and B2 valve establish a familiar household emergency pattern.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 sinking-kitchen stage ties the role reversal to A1 lifeboats and A3 flood expectation.

coach2.stated: B2 found valve can be stuck at B4; A3 flooding is anticipated disaster rather than actual rising water.
coach2.inferred: Familiar repair partners with a recurring confidence-and-panic pattern.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 answers A1 repair command with a found valve and notices A's fear.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 hands control to B2 and takes the panicked support role.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 encounters resistance while doing the role assigned at A3.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 takes control back when B4 becomes fearful and gives B the towels.
